[element-pronunciation]
=== `<pronunciation>` Pronunciation

One way to pronounce the term (<<element-term,`<term>`>>) that is being defined in a display term (<<element-term-display,`<term-display>`>>).

#### Usage/Remarks
Pronunciation elements typically have very simple content:
[source,xml]
....
   <pronunciation>trænskrɪpʃən</pronunciation>
<pronunciation>'äb-`ərs</pronunciation>
<pronunciation>//dıˈstɜ:bəns/</pronunciation>
....
This element may take the XLink attributes, so a pronunciation element can link to a sound file that pronounces the term.

#### Attributes

* <<attribute-hreflang,`@hreflang`>>
* <<attribute-specific-use,`@specific-use`>>
#### Base Attributes

* <<attribute-id,`@id`>>
* <<attribute-xml-base,`@xml:base`>>
* <<attribute-xml-lang,`@xml:lang`>> (default = en)
#### Linking Attributes

* <<attribute-xlink-actuate,`@xlink:actuate`>>
* <<attribute-xlink-href,`@xlink:href`>>
* <<attribute-xlink-role,`@xlink:role`>>
* <<attribute-xlink-show,`@xlink:show`>>
* <<attribute-xlink-title,`@xlink:title`>>
* <<attribute-xlink-type,`@xlink:type`>> (fixed value = simple)
#### Namespaces

* <<attribute-xmlns-xlink,`@xmlns:xlink`>> (fixed value = http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink)

#### Models and Context

#### May be contained in

<<element-term-display,`<term-display>`>>, <<element-term-display-string,`<term-display-string>`>>
#### Description

Any combination of: Text, numbers, or special characters <<element-bold,`<bold>`>> <<element-bold,Bold>> <<element-italic,`<italic>`>> <<element-italic,Italic>> Baseline Change Elements <<element-sub,`<sub>`>> <<element-sub,Subscript>> <<element-sup,`<sup>`>> <<element-sup,Superscript>>
#### Content Model

[source,xml]
....
<!ELEMENT  pronunciation
                        (#PCDATA %pronunciation-elements; )*        >
....
#### Expanded Content Model

(#PCDATA | bold | italic | sub | sup)*

#### Tagged Sample

##### In `<term-display>`
[source,xml]
....
...
<term-sec>
 <label>3.31</label>
 <term-display>
  <term>disturbance</term>
  <pronunciation>dɪˈstɜː.bəns</pronunciation>
  <def>
   <p>the interruption of a stable condition</p>
  </def>
 </term-display>
</term-sec>
...
....
